title: Patient Reminders, Education, and Nurse Navigation After Nephrostomy Tube Placement: A Pilot Trial
official: A Multiphase Optimization Strategy to Reduce Delays in Management of Chronic Nephrostomy Tubes
summary: People who have a nephrostomy tube placed for a blocked ureter often keep the tube for many months because they are never seen by a urologist who could treat the blockage. This pilot study tests three kinds of patient support, alone and in combination: reminder messages sent through the patient portal, an education workbook, and telephone check-ins with a nurse navigator. Adults at Henry Ford Health will be randomly assigned to one of eight combinations. The study will measure whether these supports can be delivered as planned and whether patients find them acceptable. The results will guide the design of a larger trial.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Nephrostomy tube placement or exchange at Henry Ford Health within the past 2 years
* Tube placed for current or prior ureteral obstruction
* Active MyChart patient portal account

Exclusion Criteria:

* Nephrostomy tube placed for a reason other than ureteral obstruction
* Already under the care of a urologist for the tube
* Took part in Aim 1 of this study as a focus group participant or patient advisor
